newsitem.title: NORWAY: BNbank shares surge on Fokus counterbid.
newsitem.headline: BNbank shares surge on Fokus counterbid.

text.p: Shares in Norwegian mortgage lender Bolig og Naeringsbanken (BNbank) surged 7.50 percent on Friday after a bidding war erupted in Norway's banking sector.
At 1455 GMT BNbank shares were trading 14.50 crowns up at 208 crowns in bumper turnover of 170 million crowns.
The shares, which had been trading around four percent higher on the day, jumped after Fokus Bank raised its bid for the niche group.
Fokus, Norway's fourth largest bank, raised its bid to an exchange ratio of 3.4 Fokus shares for each share in BNbank after the country's top commercial bank, Den norske Bank (DnB) made a cash offer.
On Tuesday Fokus announced it would offer 3.3 Fokus shares per BNbank share, with 20 percent of the consideration paid in cash.
DnB said on Friday it would offer a cash payment of 184.50 crowns per share, plus BNbank's 1996 dividend of 10.50 crowns, valuing BNbank at NOK 1.902 billion.
Fokus' extended valuation put the mortgage lender at 2.059 billion crowns.
